chunks: What was narrated by Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “Is there anything before the later ʿishāʾ prayer and after it?” He said: “No, except that I pray two rakʿahs after it, and I do not count them as part of salat al-layl.”

As for that which indicates the permissibility of omitting these nawāfil in cases of excuses: it is what is established of their being nawāfil, and nawāfil are that for whose omission punishment is not deserved. For if punishment were deserved for omitting them, they would be like the obligatory acts, and there would be no difference between them and those. This also indicates that.

key_terms.النَّوَافِلِ: supererogatory prayers that are not obligatory
key_terms.الْأَعْذَارِ: valid excuses or circumstances permitting omission
key_terms.الْعِقَابُ: punishment that is not incurred for leaving optional acts
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْنِ: two units of prayer performed after ʿishāʾ
key_terms.صَلَاةِ اللَّيْلِ: the night prayer, distinct here from the two rakʿahs mentioned

ai.seo_question: Can the nawāfil prayers after ʿishāʾ be omitted when one has an excuse?
ai.summary: This report states that there is no prescribed prayer before the later ʿishāʾ prayer, though Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام said that he prays two rakʿahs afterward and does not count them as part of salat al-layl. The accompanying legal discussion explains that nawāfil are optional acts whose omission does not incur punishment, and therefore they may be dropped when valid excuses exist.
